memos.headline: MSFT leads on relative strength; JPM and CAT breaking down below 50-day means
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. MSFT is the standout leader with +29.7% 12-week relative strength vs SPY, RSI 67.5 still below overbought, and only -1.3% off its 52-week high—this is a textbook momentum name I want to own, though the +23.3% premium to the 200-day mean means I'd tighten stops on any break below the 50-day (~$500). XOM is quietly strong with +12.0% 12-week relative strength, sitting just -1.5% from its high, and RSI 64 leaves room to run. On the other side, JPM's RSI at 38.3, -4.9% below its 50-day mean, and -8.4% 4-week relative strength signal a deteriorating trend I'd avoid until it reclaims ~$350. CAT is the weakest name here at -24.8% drawdown from its 52-week high, negative 12-week returns, and the highest ATR in the group at 3.17%—this is a falling knife until it can hold above its 200-day mean (~$801).

memos.headline: Mega-cap tech earnings power dominates; XOM and PG show cash-flow compression that warrants caution
memos.body: I see the strongest fundamental setups in NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, and MSFT, where revenue growth ranges from +17.7% to +105.9% YoY and net margins sit between 31% and 62%, reflecting durable and expanding earnings power. NVDA's 2027Q2 quarter is extraordinary—$96.2B in revenue (+105.9% YoY) with a 62% net margin and only $33.4B in total debt—making it the clearest earnings compounder in the universe. On the other side, XOM's Q1 net income fell 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin, and PG's fiscal Q4 showed net income declining 15.8% YoY on just 1.5% revenue growth, signaling margin erosion I'm unwilling to pay for. UNH's near-flat revenue (+0.4% YoY) and 4.9% net margin leave little room for error despite the 61% bounce in net income off a depressed base. I would need to see XOM's Q2 results and PG's margin trajectory stabilize before reconsidering those names.

views.note: Revenue +105.9% YoY, 62% net margin, and modest $33.4B debt represent the most powerful earnings trajectory in the universe.
Revenue +24.2% YoY with a 93.7% net margin (likely boosted by a one-time gain) and only $14.8B debt; even normalizing margins this is compelling.
Full-year Q4 revenue of $90B (+17.7% YoY) with 39.7% net margin and manageable $40.3B debt shows durable cloud-driven earnings growth.
Revenue $200.6B (+19.6% YoY) and net income up 244.9% to $62.7B demonstrate massive operating leverage, though $133B debt warrants monitoring.
Revenue +16.4% YoY to $109.4B with 27.2% net margin is solid, but $82.3B in total debt and slower growth vs peers temper conviction.
Revenue +24% YoY and 17.5% net margin are strong, but cyclical exposure and $36.2B debt make durability of earnings uncertain.
Net income +41.2% YoY and 36.9% margin are impressive, but $460.5B total debt and rate-cycle sensitivity limit forward visibility.
Revenue essentially flat (+0.4% YoY) with a thin 4.9% net margin; the 61% net income rebound looks like a recovery off a weak base rather than structural improvement.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on a 4.9% margin with stale Q1 data; I need to see margin stabilization before engaging.
Net income -15.8% YoY on only 1.5% revenue growth signals margin compression in a defensive name that should be delivering stability.

memos.headline: Stagflationary Tilt: 3.4% CPI and 5.24% 10y Yield Argue Against Duration and Cyclicals
memos.body: I see a regime that is best described as a hawkish pause turning into a mild re-tightening: the fed funds upper bound has risen 25bp over three months to 4.00%, while 12-month CPI is running at 3.4% — well above target — and the 10y yield has surged 110bp year-over-year to 5.24%. The labor market is stable at 4.2% unemployment (flat over 3 months, down 20bp y/y), so the Fed has no urgency to ease and may even have hiked recently. This combination of sticky inflation, rising long rates, and a positively sloped but steepening curve (+12bp 3m in the 10y-2y spread to 0.47pp) is toxic for long-duration growth equities and capital-intensive cyclicals, while modestly supportive for banks via net interest margins and for defensive staples. A CPI print falling below 3.0% or unemployment breaking above 4.5% would shift my regime call toward easing expectations and change the playbook entirely.

views.note: Long-duration consumer tech is vulnerable to a 5.24% 10y yield compressing multiples further.
High-multiple growth faces headwinds from rising real rates and no near-term easing catalyst.
Most duration-sensitive name in the universe; 110bp y/y rise in the 10y is a significant valuation drag.
Steepening curve (+12bp 3m in 10y-2y) and stable employment support NIM expansion; 4.00% fed funds keeps short-rate income healthy.
Defensive staples with pricing power should hold up in a stagflationary environment with 3.4% CPI and stable labor.
Capital-intensive cyclical faces higher borrowing costs and potential demand slowdown as policy stays restrictive at 4.00%.
Energy is a partial inflation hedge but higher rates weigh on capex-heavy upstream; I lack a strong directional view here.
Defensive characteristics help, but healthcare faces regulatory uncertainty and higher discount rates limit upside.
Consumer discretionary exposure plus long-duration AWS growth both suffer in a 5.24% 10y, 3.4% CPI environment.
Ad revenue is cyclically sensitive but strong cash generation and lower multiple than peers provide some cushion at these rates.

memos.headline: NVDA Post-Earnings Sentiment Momentum Stands Out; Limited Narrative Shifts Elsewhere in the Universe
memos.body: I see one clear sentiment signal in the universe right now: NVDA's Q2 results filed 2026-08-26 drove an +8.7% price reaction into the next close, and the company followed with two additional 8-Ks (material agreement on 8/17 and other events on 9/3), suggesting sustained positive news flow and corporate activity. That kind of clustering of filings around a strong earnings beat typically keeps media tone elevated for weeks, though by now—six weeks later—much of the positive sentiment is likely priced. Elsewhere, AAPL and AMZN both disclosed director/officer changes in early September, which are governance events that rarely shift media tone durably but can inject short-term uncertainty. CAT's entry into a material definitive agreement and creation of a direct financial obligation on 9/1 could attract negative tone if the market reads it as leveraging up, while UNH's Reg FD disclosure on 9/8 and MSFT's on 9/2 are routine investor-day-type events that I read as sentiment-neutral. I have no GDELT tone data for GOOGL, JPM, XOM, or PG in this evidence set, so I stay neutral on those names with low confidence.

views.note: Post-earnings +8.7% move and three 8-Ks in three weeks signal strong positive narrative, though six weeks on much is priced.
Director/officer change 8-K/A is governance noise, unlikely to shift media tone meaningfully.
Two September 8-Ks covering officer changes and other events are routine and sentiment-neutral.

Reg FD disclosure on 9/2 is a standard investor communication event with no discernible tone shift.

memos.headline: Surging Oil and Policy Uncertainty Signal Structural Geopolitical Stress; Favor Energy, Caution on Export-Exposed Tech
memos.body: I am struck by the divergence between a relatively calm VIX at 15.41 (down 8.8% over three months) and an economic policy uncertainty index that has spiked to 305, up 60.5% over the same period—this gap suggests markets are under-pricing a policy shock that is already visible in the data. WTI crude at $98.26, up nearly 32% in three months, points to a supply-side disruption consistent with sanctions enforcement or energy-security escalation rather than a demand-driven rally, given that HY spreads have widened 45 bps over the quarter. NVDA filed two 8-Ks in quick succession (Aug 17 and Sep 3), which I read in the context of ongoing export-control tightening toward China; until we see clarity on next-round chip restrictions, I treat this as a structural headwind. I have higher conviction on XOM benefiting from the energy-security premium and on domestically oriented names like UNH and PG, while I would be cautious on NVDA and AAPL given their China revenue exposure. A reversal in my view would require either a credible sanctions rollback or a sustained drop in the policy uncertainty index below 200.

views.note: WTI up 31.8% in three months to $98.26 reflects a geopolitical supply premium that favors integrated oil majors with domestic production.
Two 8-K filings in three weeks amid surging policy uncertainty suggest ongoing export-control headwinds on China-bound AI chip sales.
Heavy China supply-chain and revenue exposure is a liability when policy uncertainty is at 305 and rising 60% in a quarter.
Domestically oriented healthcare insurer is largely insulated from trade and energy-security disruptions; recent Reg FD filing suggests proactive investor communication.
Defensive consumer staples with pricing power and limited direct geopolitical exposure offer a hedge against the policy-uncertainty spike.
Cloud and enterprise software are less exposed to export controls than hardware, but the Sep 2 Reg FD filing and broad policy uncertainty warrant monitoring.
Infrastructure spending tailwinds are offset by rising input costs from $98 oil and potential sanctions-related supply-chain friction.
